sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我曾在凌晨4点半给总统打电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受特别优惠，网址是 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: The story of how air conditioning has become both our answer to a warming planet and a major obstacle to actually confronting it.
sentences.zh: 空调是如何成为我们应对气候变暖的方案，同时又成为我们真正面对这一问题的主要障碍的故事。

sentences.en: My colleague, Emily Badger, on the increasingly dangerous paradox of trying to control the temperature.
sentences.zh: 我的同事艾米丽·巴杰，将探讨试图控制温度所带来的日益危险的悖论。

sentences.en: Friday, August 16th.
sentences.zh: 8月16日，星期五。

sentences.en: Emily, I want to start with a very personal question for you.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽，我想先问你一个非常私人的问题。

sentences.en: What is your relationship to air conditioning?
sentences.zh: 你和空调之间是什么关系？

sentences.en: So at this exact moment, I am sitting in no air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，我正坐在没有空调的地方。

sentences.en: And it is kind of uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 感觉有点不舒服。

sentences.en: And I've turned it off because it's loud and it's not very conducive to recording a podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我把它关掉了，因为它声音很大，不太适合录制播客。

sentences.en: I didn't mean right now.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是现在。

sentences.en: I meant in the larger arc of your life.
sentences.zh: 我是指在你人生的长河中。

sentences.en: But thank you for turning it off for the purposes of this episode.
sentences.zh: 不过还是谢谢你为了这期节目把它关掉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So I grew up in Chicago in this brick three-flat apartment building, this very classic Chicago architecture, you know, built in the early 1900s.
sentences.zh: 我在芝加哥长大，住在那栋砖结构的公寓楼里，那是很典型的芝加哥建筑，你知道的，建于20世纪初。

sentences.en: And it didn't have air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 它没有空调。

sentences.en: So I didn't have air conditioning growing up.
sentences.zh: 所以我从小就没有空调。

sentences.en: Hardly anybody I knew had air conditioning growing up because we all lived in buildings like this.
sentences.zh: 我认识的人里几乎没人从小就有空调，因为我们都住在这样的建筑里。

sentences.en: Not even window units, just didn't have them.
sentences.zh: 连窗式空调都没有，就是没有。

sentences.en: Nope.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: We didn't even have a window unit in my family.
sentences.zh: 我们家里连一台窗式空调都没有。

sentences.en: And it wasn't that big of a deal in retrospect.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，这也没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: We had in this apartment these big open windows that you could open and you generate a cross breeze through them.
sentences.zh: 我们的公寓里有那种可以打开的大窗户，你可以让空气形成穿堂风。

sentences.en: And there's this kind of lovely breeze that comes off of Lake Michigan in the summer.
sentences.zh: 夏天从密歇根湖吹来的风非常宜人。

sentences.en: And when it gets really, really hot, you know, you take a cold shower at night before you get in bed.
sentences.zh: 当天气真的非常非常热时，你知道，你会在睡觉前洗个冷水澡。

sentences.en: You eat a lot of ice cream.
sentences.zh: 你会吃很多冰淇淋。

sentences.en: I can't even remember if we had air conditioning in the schools that I went to.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不记得我上学的学校里有没有空调。

sentences.en: But it just wasn't something that I thought very much about or really even experienced very much.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是我太在意或真正经历过的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You didn't miss it.
sentences.zh: 你并没有觉得缺少它。

sentences.en: You didn't even know it could be.
sentences.zh: 你甚至不知道它还能有这种功能。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And then the first job that I got out of college, I moved to Orlando.
sentences.zh: 后来我大学毕业后的第一份工作，搬到了奥兰多。

sentences.en: And totally different environment.
sentences.zh: 环境完全不同。

sentences.en: I mean, living in Florida is the story of sort of moving from one air conditioned box into another.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，住在佛罗里达就像是从一个空调房搬到另一个空调房的故事。

sentences.en: You're in your air conditioned apartment.
sentences.zh: 你待在有空调的公寓里。

sentences.en: You get in your air conditioned car.
sentences.zh: 你坐进有空调的车里。

sentences.en: You don't walk anywhere.
sentences.zh: 你哪儿也不走。

sentences.en: You drive everywhere you go.
sentences.zh: 你去哪儿都开车。

sentences.en: You drive to your air conditioned office.
sentences.zh: 你开车去有空调的办公室。

sentences.en: You go to air conditioned bars.
sentences.zh: 你去有空调的酒吧。

sentences.en: And it's really, really integral to life there in a way that was very foreign to me as someone growing up in the north.
sentences.zh: 这对那里的生活来说确实非常重要，对于在北方长大的我来说，这很陌生。

sentences.en: So you went from a dearth of air conditioning to suddenly being saturated by it.
sentences.zh: 所以你从极度缺乏空调，突然变得被空调包围了。

sentences.en: And was that a happy development?
sentences.zh: 那是一种幸福的发展吗？

sentences.en: You know, I don't think that I really gave it that much thought.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得我并没有太深思过这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, living in Orlando surrounded by air conditioning, it's just sort of that's the air that you breathe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，住在被空调包围的奥兰多，那就像是你呼吸的空气一样自然。

sentences.en: That's the way everyone lives.
sentences.zh: 那是每个人的生活方式。

sentences.en: And I think this is probably true for lots of people.
sentences.zh: 我想这对很多人来说可能都是如此。

sentences.en: We don't really give it a lot of thought.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有太去想它。

sentences.en: It's just sort of a background part of our environment.
sentences.zh: 它只是我们环境中的一种背景存在。

sentences.en: But as I have written for years now about urban policy and cities and how we live and how we develop cities,
sentences.zh: 但多年来我一直在撰写关于城市政策、城市发展以及我们如何生活和建设城市的文章，

sentences.en: it's sort of become increasingly clear to me that air conditioning is this incredibly important thing that is shaping everything around us.
sentences.zh: 我越来越清楚地认识到，空调是一件极其重要的事情，它正在塑造我们周围的一切。

sentences.en: You know, it's shaping where Americans live, where they choose to move to.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它正在塑造美国人住在哪里，他们选择搬到哪里。

sentences.en: It shapes how our houses look.
sentences.zh: 它塑造了我们房子的外观。

sentences.en: It shapes what our skylines look like.
sentences.zh: 它塑造了我们城市天际线的样子。

sentences.en: You know, it's responsible for saving lives in heat waves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它在热浪中拯救了生命。

sentences.en: In many ways, it's really improved our quality of life.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，它确实提高了我们的生活质量。

sentences.en: But it's increasingly clear to us that there are some downsides to this.
sentences.zh: 但我们越来越清楚地看到，这也有一些负面影响。

sentences.en: And one of those downsides is that while we're all sitting in our air conditioned homes and offices and cars, and we've set the thermostat to exactly 72 degrees,
sentences.zh: 其中一个负面影响是，当我们都坐在有空调的家里、办公室和车里，并将恒温器设定在正好72度时，

sentences.en: we're becoming increasingly detached from what's happening in the environment outside.
sentences.zh: 我们正变得越来越脱离外界环境正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: It is a lot easier to ignore that it's 100 degrees outside when you're sitting inside air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 当你坐在空调房里时，忽略外面100度的高温要容易得多。

sentences.en: And in some ways, I think, you know, we have forgotten how to live with heat.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为，你知道，我们已经忘记了如何与高温共存。

sentences.en: We have forgotten how to live with the climate as it existed before air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 我们已经忘记了如何与空调出现之前的气候共存。

sentences.en: And, you know, having forgotten that is probably going to cause some problems for us going forward.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，忘记了这一点可能会给我们未来的发展带来一些问题。

sentences.en: Well, Emily, what did the American landscape look like when people did have to contend with the heat in the days before air conditioning?
sentences.zh: 那么，艾米丽，在空调出现之前的日子里，当人们不得不应对高温时，美国的景观是什么样的？

sentences.en: So I think about two big things in particular.
sentences.zh: 所以我特别想到了两件大事。

sentences.en: One is that the buildings that we spend time in looked different.
sentences.zh: 一是我们花时间待的建筑看起来不同。

sentences.en: We designed houses and other kinds of buildings in ways that were really sort of thoughtfully trying to contend with the temperature outside.
sentences.zh: 我们设计房屋和其他类型的建筑时，确实是在非常用心地试图应对外界的温度。

sentences.en: And so you've got these buildings in the southwest in the United States that have these thick adobe walls that do a really good job of keeping the sun and its heat out.
sentences.zh: 所以你在美国西南部有那些厚厚的土坯墙建筑，它们在阻挡阳光和热量方面做得非常好。

sentences.en: You've got these cottages and bungalows in the southeast that are raised up off the ground so that they're not kind of receiving the heat that's absorbed by the earth.
sentences.zh: 你在东南部有那些架高的平房和别墅，这样它们就不会吸收大地传导的热量。

sentences.en: They've got big windows.
sentences.zh: 它们有大窗户。

sentences.en: They're thinking a lot about cross ventilation.
sentences.zh: 它们非常注重穿堂风。

sentences.en: They've got high ceilings so that as heat rises inside your home, you're not marinating in it while you're sitting in your living room.
sentences.zh: 它们有很高的天花板，这样当热气在室内上升时，你坐在客厅里就不会被热气熏蒸。

sentences.en: They've got front porches where people sit at the end of the day in order to try to cool off.
sentences.zh: 它们有前廊，人们在一天结束时坐在那里试图降温。

sentences.en: And then you've got the building like the one I grew up in in Chicago, which I mentioned, these sort of thick brick masonry buildings,
sentences.zh: 然后就是像我小时候在芝加哥住的那种建筑，我提到过，这些厚厚的砖石建筑，

sentences.en: which are also designed in a way that is making it possible for me to grow up in the 1980s and 90s and be okay with the fact that I don't have air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 它们的设计也让我能在80和90年代长大，并且对于家里没有空调这件事感到安之若素。

sentences.en: Because brick kind of retains cool air.
sentences.zh: 因为砖块可以保留凉爽的空气。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: And so part of what results from all of this is that the buildings in Georgia look different from the buildings in Arizona, look different from the buildings in Chicago,
sentences.zh: 所以这一切带来的结果之一就是，佐治亚州的建筑看起来与亚利桑那州的建筑不同，与芝加哥的建筑也不同，

sentences.en: because in each of those places, we're designing buildings that react to the particular climate in those environments.
sentences.zh: 因为在每一个地方，我们都在设计能够应对当地特定气候的建筑。

sentences.en: And so this is the first big change.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一个重大变化。

sentences.en: Think of a time when you have to design a building to interact with what's going on outside, with how humid it is, with how hot it gets.
sentences.zh: 想想看，当你必须设计一座建筑来与外界环境互动时，要考虑湿度如何，温度有多高。

sentences.en: But the other thing that was very different in the pre-air conditioning environment is that there were just a lot fewer people living in the parts of the United States that were really hot and swampy.
sentences.zh: 但空调出现之前的环境中，另一个非常不同的地方是，居住在美国那些真正炎热潮湿地区的人要少得多。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's kind of incredible to think about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这有点难以置信。

sentences.en: But like 1940, there are fewer people living in the state of Florida than living in the state of Arkansas.
sentences.zh: 比如1940年，佛罗里达州居住的人口比阿肯色州还要少。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: There are about 8,000 people total living in the city of Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 拉斯维加斯市总共只有大约8000人居住。

sentences.en: Dallas and Houston are nowhere to be found on the list of the largest cities in America.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯和休斯顿在当时美国最大城市名单上根本找不到。

sentences.en: So fundamentally, before air conditioning, there just aren't a lot of people living in places where it is uncomfortable if you're not controlling the temperature in some way.
sentences.zh: 所以从根本上说，在空调出现之前，并没有多少人住在那些如果不以某种方式控制温度就会让人感到不舒服的地方。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If it's too hot, then you just don't live there.
sentences.zh: 如果太热，那你就不住在那儿。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So climate shapes your decisions about where to live.
sentences.zh: 所以气候决定了你关于居住地的选择。

sentences.en: It shapes your decisions about how to build housing.
sentences.zh: 它决定了你关于如何建造房屋的选择。

sentences.en: It shapes your decisions about where to spend your time in your house.
sentences.zh: 它决定了你关于在家里如何消磨时间的选择。

sentences.en: Maybe you go on to your front porch in the evening when it's cooling down.
sentences.zh: 也许傍晚天气凉快下来时，你会去前廊坐坐。

sentences.en: You know, in many ways, our behavior is shaped by the climate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在很多方面，我们的行为都是由气候塑造的。

sentences.en: And then air conditioning comes along,
sentences.zh: 然后空调出现了，

sentences.en: and it totally changes everything that I've been talking about because now the outdoor climate doesn't really affect what your life is like indoors.
sentences.zh: 它彻底改变了我所谈论的一切，因为现在室外气候对你的室内生活几乎没有影响了。

sentences.en: Just tell us about that moment because I don't think any of us really know the story.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲那个时刻吧，因为我觉得我们中没人真正了解这个故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, there have been contraptions invented in the 1900s that were trying to do things like blow forced air over big blocks of ice in order to cool it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，20世纪发明了一些装置，试图通过在大冰块上吹强制空气来降温。

sentences.en: But the thing that we really think of as air conditioning is just totally a 20th century story.
sentences.zh: 但我们真正认为的空调，完全是一个20世纪的故事。

sentences.en: It starts at the very beginning of the 20th century in 1902 when Willis Carrier invents this machine.
sentences.zh: 它始于20世纪初的1902年，当时威利斯·开利发明了这种机器。

sentences.en: It's kind of controlling the temperature and the humidity and the purity of air, particularly in an industrial context.
sentences.zh: 它主要是在工业背景下控制温度、湿度和空气纯度。

sentences.en: You know, the very first use of this in 1902 is in a printing plant.
sentences.zh: 你知道，1902年它最初的用途是在一家印刷厂。

sentences.en: And fundamentally, the problem that it's solving is that the moisture content in the air is really sort of becoming a problem for printing documents.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，它解决的问题是空气中的水分含量对印刷文件造成了困扰。

sentences.en: You're saying basically publishing, journalism, is responsible for air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 你是说基本上是出版业、新闻业促成了空调的诞生。

sentences.en: Yes, everybody can thank us, and then later they can blame us.
sentences.zh: 是的，每个人都可以感谢我们，后来他们也可以责怪我们。

sentences.en: And so in the beginning, what air conditioning is doing is it's sort of solving an industrial problem.
sentences.zh: 所以起初，空调的作用是解决工业问题。

sentences.en: The machines are hot, or maybe it's a textile mill and too much humidity is sort of destroying your textiles.
sentences.zh: 机器很热，或者如果是纺织厂，湿度过大会损坏纺织品。

sentences.en: And also, you know, you want your workers to be productive in these manufacturing spaces.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你希望工人在这些制造空间里保持高效率。

sentences.en: Lots of people in a small space with hot machines, right?
sentences.zh: 狭小的空间里有很多人和发热的机器，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, and so in the very beginning of the 20th century, it's not about providing comfort for people.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以在20世纪初，它并不是为了给人们提供舒适。

sentences.en: It's about conditioning the environments that manufacturing and industry is happening.
sentences.zh: 它是为了调节制造业和工业发生的空间环境。

sentences.en: And then it is this very sort of long story that plays out over several decades where this invention moves from these industrial spaces into these other kinds of spaces.
sentences.zh: 然后这是一个跨越几十年的漫长故事，这项发明从这些工业空间进入了其他类型的空间。

sentences.en: Yes, you lucky people, just sit back for a moment, relax, and notice the delightfully clean, cool, and refreshing atmosphere of this scientifically air-conditioned theater.
sentences.zh: 是的，你们这些幸运的人，请坐下来放松一下，感受一下这个经过科学空调处理的剧院里那令人愉悦、凉爽、清新的空气。

sentences.en: Great, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 很棒，不是吗？

sentences.en: So then it comes into theaters and becomes almost this marketing tool to attract people inside.
sentences.zh: 所以它进入了剧院，几乎成了吸引人们入内的营销工具。

sentences.en: You can enjoy great motion picture entertainment all summer long in cool comfort.
sentences.zh: 整个夏天，您都可以在凉爽舒适的环境中享受精彩的电影娱乐。

sentences.en: Go see a movie and enjoy air-conditioning while you're in there.
sentences.zh: 去看场电影，享受里面的空调吧。

sentences.en: Yes, low-cost, all-season air-conditioning is the right kind for you.
sentences.zh: 是的，低成本、全天候的空调才是适合您的选择。

sentences.en: And you're so right to choose a 55 Rambler cross-country.
sentences.zh: 您选择55款兰博跨界车真是太对了。

sentences.en: And then at the same time, you know, cars in America that have air-conditioning in them, the share of those cars is rising and rising.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，你知道，美国汽车中配备空调的比例也在不断上升。

sentences.en: It moves into office buildings.
sentences.zh: 它进入了办公楼。

sentences.en: Instead of traveling away from business and home to seek relief, you can obtain this same comfort right in your own home or office through air-conditioning.
sentences.zh: 与其为了寻求凉爽而远离工作和家，您可以通过空调在自己的家里或办公室获得同样的舒适。

sentences.en: And then eventually, after sort of decades of refining this technology, and it gets smaller, and it gets more affordable, and it becomes more advanced.
sentences.zh: 最终，在经过几十年的技术改进后，它变得更小、更实惠、更先进。

sentences.en: This lucky baby will sleep quietly through the night.
sentences.zh: 这个幸运的宝宝将整晚安静地入睡。

sentences.en: It reaches the American home.
sentences.zh: 它走进了美国家庭。

sentences.en: And we get the window unit.
sentences.zh: 我们有了窗式空调。

sentences.en: This baby's RCA air conditioner will keep his room filled with cool, dry, fresh air.
sentences.zh: 这个宝宝的RCA空调将让他的房间充满凉爽、干燥、清新的空气。

sentences.en: And the window unit is this much more affordable, portable, easy to pick up at the store, bring to your house.
sentences.zh: 窗式空调要实惠得多，便携，容易在商店买到，带回家。

sentences.en: You don't need to get a special installer.
sentences.zh: 你不需要找专门的安装人员。

sentences.en: You stick it in your window.
sentences.zh: 你把它插在窗户上就行了。

sentences.en: And now, all of a sudden, you're getting all of these benefits of humidity-controlled, temperature-controlled air inside of your home.
sentences.zh: 现在，突然之间，你就能在家里享受到所有这些湿度可控、温度可控的空气带来的好处了。

sentences.en: Humidity-controlled, dust and pollen filtered.
sentences.zh: 湿度受控，过滤了灰尘和花粉。

sentences.en: My indoor climate is always perfect.
sentences.zh: 我的室内气候总是完美无缺。

sentences.en: At that point, it's off to the races.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，一切就全速运转起来了。

sentences.en: It sort of takes over the American home.
sentences.zh: 它几乎接管了美国家庭。

sentences.en: And we can sort of see in census data, for instance, that by about the start of the 1970s,
sentences.zh: 例如，我们可以从人口普查数据中看出，大约在 20 世纪 70 年代初，

sentences.en: about half of all new single-family homes that are built in America have air-conditioning in them.
sentences.zh: 美国新建的单户住宅中，约有一半安装了空调。

sentences.en: And the other thing that we see in census data at this time is that Americans themselves are starting to move to places that are really hot, like Florida, like Texas, like Arizona,
sentences.zh: 我们在当时的人口普查数据中看到的另一件事是，美国人自己开始搬到非常炎热的地方，比如佛罗里达州、德克萨斯州、亚利桑那州，

sentences.en: like Nevada, places that were kind of uninhabitable before air-conditioning.
sentences.zh: 还有内华达州，这些地方在空调普及之前几乎是不适合居住的。

sentences.en: Now they're booming in population.
sentences.zh: 现在它们的人口正在激增。

sentences.en: And there was this wonderful editorial that was actually published in the Times in 1970 about the census that year.
sentences.zh: 1970 年《泰晤士报》曾发表过一篇关于当年人口普查的精彩社论。

sentences.en: And how 1970 was like the air-conditioning census.
sentences.zh: 文中提到 1970 年的人口普查就像是一次“空调普查”。

sentences.en: And it refers to how air-conditioning had become this really powerful influence for circulating people as well as air in this country.
sentences.zh: 它指出空调已成为在这个国家循环人口和空气的强大推动力。

sentences.en: And this is a story that continues like right up until this day where air-conditioning is sort of extending its reach into every corner of the country, you know,
sentences.zh: 这个故事一直延续至今，空调的影响力几乎延伸到了这个国家的每一个角落，你知道的，

sentences.en: every sort of housing type.
sentences.zh: 每一种住房类型。

sentences.en: And today, about two-thirds of American households in this country have central air.
sentences.zh: 如今，美国约有三分之二的家庭拥有中央空调。

sentences.en: And about 90 percent, so nine in ten of them, have some kind of air-conditioning if we include things like window units.
sentences.zh: 如果算上窗式空调等设备，约有 90%，即十分之九的家庭拥有某种形式的空调。

sentences.en: And if we look just at new housing that's built in America today, looking back in 2023, about 98 percent of new single-family homes in America had air-conditioning.
sentences.zh: 如果我们只看美国今天建造的新房，回顾 2023 年，约 98% 的新建单户住宅都配备了空调。

sentences.en: I mean, what you're talking about is basically 200 or so million air-conditioning units, condensers, boxes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你所说的基本上是 2 亿台左右的空调机组、冷凝器和机箱。

sentences.en: That's a lot.
sentences.zh: 那可真是个庞大的数字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And as air-conditioning has extended its reach into every corner of the country, into so many of the buildings where we spend time,
sentences.zh: 随着空调的触角延伸到全国的每一个角落，延伸到我们花费大量时间所在的众多建筑中，

sentences.en: I think it becomes clear that we've really kind of engineered our modern lives entirely around it.
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显，我们已经完全围绕它来构建了我们的现代生活。

sentences.en: And our reliance on this technology going forward is both unsustainable, and in fact, it's put a lot of people in a very vulnerable position.
sentences.zh: 我们对这项技术的依赖在未来既是不可持续的，事实上，它也让许多人处于非常脆弱的境地。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是 Winnalou。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是 Sam Mazursky，我每天负责创作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 即可开始游戏。

sentences.en: Emily, walk us through how our reliance on air-conditioning is both, as you just said, unsustainable and perhaps even kind of dangerous to us.
sentences.zh: Emily，请为我们梳理一下，为什么我们对空调的依赖正如你刚才所说，既不可持续，甚至可能对我们有害？

sentences.en: So the first obvious thing that it does is it just requires an enormous amount of energy for so many people to be air-conditioning so many spaces all the time.
sentences.zh: 首先显而易见的一点是，要让这么多人一直为空调空间降温，需要消耗巨大的能源。

sentences.en: And so to sort of think about this in a larger sense, our buildings in the United States are responsible for about 30% of the greenhouse gas emissions.
sentences.zh: 从更宏观的角度来看，美国的建筑排放了约 30% 的温室气体。

sentences.en: And that refers to the fossil fuels that we burn directly to heat and cool buildings and to cook in them,
sentences.zh: 这指的是我们直接燃烧化石燃料来为建筑供暖、制冷和烹饪，

sentences.en: but also to generate the electricity that then allows us to do things like plug in our window units.
sentences.zh: 同时也包括发电，从而让我们能够使用窗式空调等设备。

sentences.en: So there's a ton of energy use happening here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里消耗了大量的能源。

sentences.en: But part of what's also happening is that all of these buildings have been fundamentally designed to consume lots of energy.
sentences.zh: 但部分原因还在于，所有这些建筑在设计之初就是为了消耗大量能源。

sentences.en: A lot of these buildings were built during a time, you know, in the 50s and the 60s and in more recent years where energy was cheap.
sentences.zh: 许多建筑建于 50 年代、60 年代以及更近的时期，那时能源价格低廉。

sentences.en: The idea that you're designing a building that demands lots of energy, who cares?
sentences.zh: 设计一栋需要大量能源的建筑又有什么关系呢？

sentences.en: We're not paying a ton of money for the energy.
sentences.zh: 我们又不用为能源支付高昂的费用。

sentences.en: And in the 60s and in the 50s, we weren't particularly thinking about whether or not using energy is going to cause climate change.
sentences.zh: 而且在 50 和 60 年代，我们并没有特别考虑使用能源是否会导致气候变化。

sentences.en: So because of this, we get this glut of inefficient houses.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们得到了大量低效的房屋。

sentences.en: And this happens not just with houses, but with everything in the built environment.
sentences.zh: 这种情况不仅发生在住宅上，也发生在建筑环境中的一切事物上。

sentences.en: Think about strip malls, shopping centers, workplaces, even offices.
sentences.zh: 想想商业街、购物中心、工作场所，甚至是办公室。

sentences.en: This sort of ubiquitous, tall, boxy, glass-covered office building that we think about in cities all over the country, all over the world.
sentences.zh: 这种我们在全国乃至全世界城市中随处可见的、高大、方正、玻璃覆盖的办公楼。

sentences.en: This is a building that is born out of the air conditioning age.
sentences.zh: 这就是诞生于空调时代的建筑。

sentences.en: That glassy box is designed around air conditioning such that, you know, without air conditioning, those kinds of offices don't make sense.
sentences.zh: 那种玻璃盒子是围绕空调设计的，以至于如果没有空调，这些办公室根本无法运作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about the office that you and I call home, the New York Times high-rise building in Midtown.
sentences.zh: 我想到你我称之为“家”的那个办公室，位于中城的《纽约时报》高层建筑。

sentences.en: That does not feel, for all its virtues, like a building you'd want to be in without air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 尽管它有种种优点，但如果没有空调，你绝对不会想待在那栋楼里。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: It's glass and tall, and I think it'd be very hot.
sentences.zh: 它又高又全是玻璃，我想里面会非常热。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, when you think about tall glass office buildings, they're basically greenhouses if you're not controlling the air inside.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你想到那些高大的玻璃办公楼时，如果你不控制内部空气，它们基本上就是温室。

sentences.en: They're designed such that not only do you not have to open a window in order to cool off, you couldn't open a window even if you wanted to.
sentences.zh: 它们的设计使得你不仅不需要开窗降温，甚至就算你想开也开不了。

sentences.en: These buildings don't have windows that open because they're designed to be these hermetically sealed environments where we're going to keep the outside climate out and we're going to control the climate on the inside.
sentences.zh: 这些建筑没有可以打开的窗户，因为它们被设计成密封的环境，我们要把外部气候挡在外面，并控制内部气候。

sentences.en: And this idea that the outside doesn't matter is true in the design of so many of our buildings, our offices, even our homes,
sentences.zh: 这种“外部环境无关紧要”的理念在我们的许多建筑、办公室甚至住宅的设计中都是真实的，

sentences.en: and that actually puts people into an incredibly vulnerable situation.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上让人们陷入了极其脆弱的境地。

sentences.en: And vulnerable how exactly?
sentences.zh: 脆弱是指什么？

sentences.en: So let's assume a storm comes through and the power goes out, or your air conditioning stops working because you've been running it all the time all summer long,
sentences.zh: 假设一场风暴来袭导致停电，或者因为你整个夏天都在不停地运行空调导致它坏了，

sentences.en: or when we have these extreme heat conditions and the electric utility tells you, please try to preserve the amount of air conditioning that you're using.
sentences.zh: 又或者当我们遇到极端高温天气，电力公司要求你尽量减少空调使用量时。

sentences.en: What happens when all of a sudden millions of people who have been living in an environment designed entirely around air conditioning can't have that air conditioning?
sentences.zh: 当数百万一直生活在完全围绕空调设计的环境中的人突然无法使用空调时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Like, we start to see real probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到真正的问题了。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is an abstract.
sentences.zh: 而且，这并非抽象的概念。

sentences.en: Like, we have actually seen this happen in the United States even this year, in other recent years,
sentences.zh: 我们实际上在美国甚至今年以及其他近几年都亲眼目睹了这种情况，

sentences.en: where terrible storms have ripped through the state of Texas and millions of people have been left without power.
sentences.zh: 可怕的风暴席卷了德克萨斯州，数百万人在断电的情况下生活。

sentences.en: And when this happens in the middle of a heat wave, people die.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生在热浪期间，就会有人死亡。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that seems like an example of the multiple ways that air conditioning conspires to make us avoid contending with the realities of heat.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个例子，说明了空调如何以多种方式合谋让我们逃避面对高温的现实。

sentences.en: To return to this idea you introduced earlier on, AC allows more people to go to a place like Texas than they'd ever go if there weren't AC making them comfortable.
sentences.zh: 回到你之前提到的观点，空调让更多人能够前往像德克萨斯州这样的地方，如果不是空调让他们感到舒适，他们绝不会去那里。

sentences.en: And to design and live in homes and offices that become a cauldron without air conditioning when it fails.
sentences.zh: 并设计和居住在一旦空调失效就会变成大锅的房屋和办公室里。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, air conditioning makes it possible for people to believe that you could be comfortable in Texas in the summer, in Arizona in the summer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，空调让人们相信在夏天待在德克萨斯州或亚利桑那州是可以很舒适的。

sentences.en: And so people move to these places in large numbers.
sentences.zh: 于是人们大量涌入这些地方。

sentences.en: And then when the air conditioning fails,
sentences.zh: 然后当空调失效时，

sentences.en: they're sort of suddenly thrust into a world where they're living in the middle of the Arizona desert or they're living in the middle of Texas on a 110-degree day.
sentences.zh: 他们突然被推入一个世界，生活在亚利桑那沙漠中心，或者在 110 华氏度（约 43 摄氏度）的高温下生活在德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: And that could be life-threatening.
sentences.zh: 那可能会危及生命。

sentences.en: Especially with climate change making it even hotter in these places, it doesn't really seem sustainable for a lot of people to live in those places without air conditioning,
sentences.zh: 特别是在气候变化导致这些地方变得更热的情况下，对于许多人来说，如果没有空调，没有某种人工调节环境的手段，住在这些地方似乎确实不可持续。

sentences.en: without some kind of artificial tempering of the environment.
sentences.zh: 没有某种人工的环境调节。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's not just because of the heat.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且不仅仅是因为高温。

sentences.en: I mean, is it sustainable for a metropolitan area of 5 million people to exist in Phoenix in the middle of the desert when there's also not enough water there for everyone?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当凤凰城的水资源也不足以供应每个人时，一个拥有 500 万人口的都市区存在于沙漠中心，这真的可持续吗？

sentences.en: You know, so air conditioning sort of lulls people into moving to these places, which might be problematic for lots of other reasons as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，空调诱使人们搬到这些地方，这可能在其他许多方面也存在问题。

sentences.en: But we've sort of convinced ourselves that the climate doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 但我们已经说服自己，气候并不重要。

sentences.en: We're going to control it.
sentences.zh: 我们要控制它。

sentences.en: We're going to engineer our way into living with it.
sentences.zh: 我们要通过工程手段来适应它。

sentences.en: You're reminding me, Emily, of an episode we did on the show about this very idea.
sentences.zh: Emily，你让我想起了我们在节目中做过的一期关于这个想法的节目。

sentences.en: It focused on the water shortage in Arizona and the plans to pipe in and, as I recall, desalinate ocean water to deal with the problem of not enough water in Arizona.
sentences.zh: 它关注的是亚利桑那州的水资源短缺，以及为了解决亚利桑那州缺水问题而计划引入并（我记得是）淡化海水。

sentences.en: And it doesn't really seem fathomable that that proposition would ever occur to people if they weren't living there in the comfort of air conditioning in the first place.
sentences.zh: 如果人们最初不是生活在空调的舒适中，很难想象他们会产生这种想法。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I mean, there have been people living in the region of Phoenix for centuries.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，几个世纪以来一直有人居住在凤凰城地区。

sentences.en: So it's not that nobody can ever live there.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说没人能住在那里。

sentences.en: But what air conditioning does is it enables millions of people to live there who don't actually want to contend with 100-degree temperatures all summer long.
sentences.zh: 但空调的作用是让数百万实际上并不想在整个夏天忍受 100 华氏度（约 38 摄氏度）高温的人能够住在那里。

sentences.en: So a place like Phoenix then becomes this perfect example where we now have 5 million people living in the middle of the Arizona desert,
sentences.zh: 所以像凤凰城这样的地方就成了完美的例子，现在有 500 万人生活在亚利桑那沙漠的中心，

sentences.en: and they all have this expectation of comfort there.
sentences.zh: 他们对那里都有舒适的期望。

sentences.en: That any environment that I move into, in my home, in my office, in my car, I should be encased in this sort of cooling, calm, 72-degree, humidity-controlled environment.
sentences.zh: 无论我进入什么环境，在家里、办公室还是车里，我都应该被包裹在这种凉爽、平静、72 华氏度（约 22 摄氏度）、湿度受控的环境中。

sentences.en: And that sense of comfort becomes so deeply entrenched kind of culturally, and this isn't just about Phoenix, this is about sort of all of us.
sentences.zh: 这种舒适感在文化上变得根深蒂固，这不仅仅是关于凤凰城，这是关于我们所有人。

sentences.en: I think we have set up an expectation or even an entitlement around comfort such that it makes it really difficult to start to ask people,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们已经建立了一种关于舒适的期望，甚至是一种权利感，以至于很难开始问人们，

sentences.en: do you really need to turn up your air conditioning today?
sentences.zh: 你今天真的需要把空调开得那么大吗？

sentences.en: So that makes me wonder how people are ever going to get off the air conditioning hamster wheel that we're describing here.
sentences.zh: 这让我好奇人们将如何摆脱我们所描述的这种空调“仓鼠轮”。

sentences.en: I mean, why would anyone?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么会有人想摆脱呢？

sentences.en: Well, we have to figure out how to do something if we want to address climate change, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果我们想应对气候变化，我们必须想办法做点什么，对吧？

sentences.en: So there are a number of different things that are going to happen here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里会发生许多不同的事情。

sentences.en: Air conditioning is going to become more efficient.
sentences.zh: 空调会变得更高效。

sentences.en: We're going to have more renewable energy sources to power it in the future.
sentences.zh: 未来我们将有更多的可再生能源来驱动它。

sentences.en: And I think we're increasingly going to see architects and builders trying to rediscover these lost ideas that we used to have about how to design buildings with the climate in mind,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们将越来越多地看到建筑师和建筑商试图重新发现我们过去关于如何考虑气候来设计建筑的失传理念，

sentences.en: you know, how to shade them, how to ventilate them in a more natural way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如何遮阳，如何以更自然的方式通风。

sentences.en: But I also have talked to some people who say that all of that is not going to be enough.
sentences.zh: 但我也和一些人谈过，他们说所有这些都是不够的。

sentences.en: One of them is Daniel Barber, who's an architectural historian who has thought a lot about life after air conditioning,
sentences.zh: 其中一位是 Daniel Barber，他是一位建筑历史学家，对空调之后的生活思考了很多，

sentences.en: or as he puts it, after comfort, you know, life in a world where we're not depending on air conditioning so much.
sentences.zh: 或者正如他所说，在“舒适之后”，你知道，生活在一个我们不再那么依赖空调的世界里。

sentences.en: And the point that he makes is that there are difficult things and changes that we would have to do going forward.
sentences.zh: 他提出的观点是，未来我们将不得不面对困难的事情并做出改变。

sentences.en: If we know that our buildings are responsible for a lot of greenhouse gas emissions, our dependence on air conditioning is responsible for a large share of that.
sentences.zh: 如果我们知道我们的建筑排放了大量的温室气体，我们对空调的依赖就是其中的很大一部分原因。

sentences.en: And we have to reduce it in some way.
sentences.zh: 我们必须以某种方式减少它。

sentences.en: Like what we all need to do is change our own behavior.
sentences.zh: 比如我们都需要做的是改变我们自己的行为。

sentences.en: We need to sort of think anew about our relationship to comfort.
sentences.zh: 我们需要重新思考我们与舒适的关系。

sentences.en: And are we willing to be uncomfortable some of the time?
sentences.zh: 我们是否愿意在某些时候感到不舒服？

sentences.en: Am I willing to wait until July to turn my air conditioning on?
sentences.zh: 我是否愿意等到七月才打开空调？

sentences.en: Am I willing to turn it off at night when it's not really necessary to use it?
sentences.zh: 我是否愿意在晚上不需要的时候关掉它？

sentences.en: Am I willing to sleep at 80 degrees instead of 72 degrees?
sentences.zh: 我是否愿意在 80 华氏度（约 27 摄氏度）而不是 72 华氏度（约 22 摄氏度）下睡觉？

sentences.en: Or 68?
sentences.zh: 或者 68 华氏度（约 20 摄氏度）？

sentences.en: Or 68 or 65.
sentences.zh: 或者 68 华氏度或 65 华氏度（约 18 摄氏度）。

sentences.en: 65, and he's talking about asking people to do something really difficult.
sentences.zh: 65 华氏度，他谈到的是要求人们做一些非常困难的事情。

sentences.en: He is asking people to be uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 他是在要求人们去忍受不适。

sentences.en: You are, of course, by conveying this message, putting this problem on individuals, not governments, not states.
sentences.zh: 你当然是通过传达这个信息，把这个问题推给了个人，而不是政府，也不是国家。

sentences.en: And lots of people might hear this and think the real solutions have to come from regulators, have to come from institutions,
sentences.zh: 很多人听到这个可能会认为真正的解决方案必须来自监管机构，必须来自机构，

sentences.en: have to come from the people who have a lot more control over how this all works.
sentences.zh: 必须来自那些对这一切运作方式有更多控制权的人。

sentences.en: I think that there are some ways in which that will happen, too.
sentences.zh: 我认为在某些方面这也会发生。

sentences.en: When we think about new buildings that are being designed or renovated today that are trying to adopt some of these techniques to be less reliant on indoor air conditioning,
sentences.zh: 当我们想到今天正在设计或翻新的新建筑，试图采用其中一些技术以减少对室内空调的依赖时，

sentences.en: they're often institutional buildings.
sentences.zh: 它们通常是机构建筑。

sentences.en: You will see cities commit to when we rebuild our schools, when we build a new library, when we build a new civic center,
sentences.zh: 你会看到城市承诺，当我们重建学校、建造新图书馆、建造新市民中心时，

sentences.en: we are going to embody these things that we are asking other people to do, too.
sentences.zh: 我们将体现这些我们也在要求其他人做的事情。

sentences.en: And obviously, there are government incentives in the United States, for instance, to better insulate your home, to do things that would make your home greener.
sentences.zh: 显然，美国政府也有激励措施，例如更好地为你的房屋隔热，做一些让你的房屋更环保的事情。

sentences.en: So there's certainly a role for government.
sentences.zh: 所以政府肯定有其作用。

sentences.en: But what Daniel Barber at least would argue is that we all bear some responsibility.
sentences.zh: 但至少 Daniel Barber 会认为，我们每个人都承担着一定的责任。

sentences.en: And air conditioning has lulled us into thinking that we're not impacted by how hot it is outside.
sentences.zh: 空调让我们以为自己不受室外温度的影响。

sentences.en: But it's also maybe lulled us into thinking like,
sentences.zh: 但也可能让我们以为，

sentences.en: I'm not the one who needs to particularly change my behavior in any way.
sentences.zh: 我不是那个特别需要以任何方式改变行为的人。

sentences.en: But fundamentally, what we're talking about is people embracing a kind of different cultural idea about what it means to be comfortable.
sentences.zh: 但从根本上说，我们谈论的是人们拥抱一种关于“舒适意味着什么”的不同文化理念。

sentences.en: The idea that existing in a room that is artificially cooled to 68 to 72 degrees Fahrenheit, that that's the ideal temperature.
sentences.zh: 那种认为待在人工冷却到 68 到 72 华氏度的房间里就是理想温度的想法。

sentences.en: That's not like some true fact about the human body.
sentences.zh: 那并不是关于人体的某种真理。

sentences.en: That's like a cultural idea that's been created over decades by the air conditioning industry, by architects and builders and culture and shopping malls and movie theaters.
sentences.zh: 那是由空调行业、建筑师、建筑商、文化、购物中心和电影院在几十年间创造出来的一种文化理念。

sentences.en: And the idea that comfort means this one particular thing is an idea that we have constructed ourselves.
sentences.zh: 认为舒适意味着这一特定事物的想法，是我们自己构建出来的。

sentences.en: And so, you know, what if we culturally came up with a different idea about comfort?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果我们从文化上提出一种关于舒适的不同想法会怎样？

sentences.en: What if more people came to accept the idea that going and sitting out on my front porch in the evening is where I get comfort from?
sentences.zh: 如果更多人开始接受这样一个想法：晚上坐在前廊上就是我获得舒适感的方式呢？

sentences.en: And it's also, by the way, like how I interact with my neighbors.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这也是我与邻居互动的方式。

sentences.en: And I had stopped doing that when we were all retreating inside to air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 而当我们都退缩到空调房里时，我就停止了那样做。

sentences.en: What if we revived the idea that it's actually quite lovely in the summertime to sleep with an open window and to have fresh air?
sentences.zh: 如果我们恢复那种“在夏天开着窗睡觉并呼吸新鲜空气其实非常美好”的想法会怎样？

sentences.en: You know, it's not impossible to change ideas about this because we created these ideas in the first place.
sentences.zh: 你知道，改变关于这个的想法并非不可能，因为这些想法本身就是我们创造出来的。

sentences.en: Well, Emily, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，艾米丽，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Thursday, the White House said that its newfound authority to use the Medicare program to negotiate prices of prescription drugs with pharmaceutical companies
sentences.zh: 周四，白宫表示，其新获得的利用联邦医疗保险计划与制药公司协商处方药价格的权力，

sentences.en: is likely to save taxpayers about $6 billion a year.
sentences.zh: 预计每年可为纳税人节省约60亿美元。

sentences.en: That power came from President Biden's Inflation Reduction Act, which became law two years ago.
sentences.zh: 这项权力源于拜登总统两年前签署成为法律的《通胀削减法案》。

sentences.en: Under it, regulators have now lowered the price of widely used treatments, including blood thinners and medications for arthritis and diabetes, some by up to 79%.
sentences.zh: 根据该法案，监管机构现已降低了多种常用药物的价格，包括血液稀释剂以及治疗关节炎和糖尿病的药物，部分降幅高达79%。

sentences.en: And both vice presidential nominees, Minnesota Governor Tim Walz and Ohio Senator J.D.
sentences.zh: 两位副总统候选人，明尼苏达州州长蒂姆·沃尔兹和俄亥俄州参议员J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, have agreed to debate each other on October 1st during a televised face-off hosted by CBS News.
sentences.zh: 万斯，已同意于10月1日在哥伦比亚广播公司新闻部主办的电视辩论中进行交锋。

sentences.en: That means there will be three debates before Election Day, one vice presidential debate and two presidential debates between Donald Trump and Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在选举日之前将有三场辩论，一场副总统辩论，以及唐纳德·特朗普与卡玛拉·哈里斯之间的两场总统辩论。

sentences.en: Finally, remember to catch a new episode of The Interview right here tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 最后，别忘了明天准时收看《访谈》节目的新一期内容。

sentences.en: This week, David Marchese speaks with the singer Jelly Roll about addiction, recovery, and putting his whole self into his music.
sentences.zh: 本周，大卫·马尔凯塞将与歌手Jelly Roll畅谈成瘾、康复以及他如何全身心地投入到音乐创作中。

sentences.en: I think of everything as a going-out-of-business sale, and I give everything I got, everything I do, every time I do it right now.
sentences.zh: 我把每一件事都看作是最后一次机会，所以我现在所做的每一件事，每一次都会倾尽全力。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Shannon Lynn and Diana Nguyen, with help from Michael Simon-Johnson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由香农·林恩和戴安娜·阮制作，迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊提供了协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Devin Taylor, contains research help from Susan Lee, original music by Marion Lozano,
sentences.zh: 节目由德文·泰勒剪辑，苏珊·李提供了研究支持，原创音乐由马里昂·洛萨诺、

sentences.en: Dan Powell,
sentences.zh: 丹·鲍威尔、

sentences.en: Rory Nemisto, and Will Reed, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 罗里·内米斯托和威尔·里德创作，音频工程由艾丽莎·莫克斯利负责。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备假期接待客人的相关内容。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们需要全黑的睡眠环境吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是他们是否会喝到断片才睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们是否有过敏或食物不耐受的情况？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app, or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。

sentences.en: Or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 或者在任何你喜欢的平台上收听。
